issues.finding: The proposition merely requires the four named connectives to occur in L, but concludes value agreement for every formula. Earlier formation rules also admit nullary constants and arbitrary extra connectives, whose truth functions are not constrained here; the induction proves only the fragment generated by variables and the four named connectives. The displayed valuation condition is also intended for every propositional variable.
issues.proposed_resolution: State in the target that the language has only the four named connectives and no propositional constants, and quantify the Boolean-valued condition over every propositional variable. This restricts the corollary to that fully proved language fragment.

issues.finding: The proof writes a valuation on the left of the semantic-entailment symbol for both Gamma and not-B. These are satisfaction and negated-satisfaction assertions about the chosen valuation, not entailment assertions.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use pSat_v(Gamma)[L] and its slash-negated form pSat/_v(B)[L] in the target and bounded comparison view.

translation_treatment: The target translates Boolean-restricted truth-function agreement, the induction and its corollary while narrowing the language to the fragment the induction covers and correcting the countermodel satisfaction notation. Frozen source is unchanged.
